thread:
Mia Chen: FYI I opened a PR with a small SDK example and some test cases for quota headers — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1423. It demonstrates reading X-Quota-Remaining / X-Quota-Reset and a defensive fallback for missing headers. This is a backcompat testrun for docs that reference metering headers.
Samir Patel: digging in now. what harness did you use to validate?
Mia Chen: local postman + python snippet under /dev/samples; unit tests run with `make docs-test`. snippet in the PR: 
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_API_KEY'))
resp = client.requests.post('/v1/text/generate', json={'prompt':'hi'})
quota = resp.headers.get('X-Quota-Remaining')
if quota is None:
    # assume unlimited / fallback path
    quota_left = -1
else:
    quota_left = int(quota)
```
Samir Patel: CI flagged failure on one of the new tests: `quota_burst_retention` fails intermittently on macos-latest. stack points to int(None) when header missing.
Alex Romero: can we change the snippet to be more defensive (e.g., `int(resp.headers.get('X-Quota-Remaining','-1'))`) and include a short paragraph that headers are optional depending on deployment?
Mia Chen: yep. plan: 1) update example to defensive parse, 2) add note in docs about which deployments provide quota headers, 3) add unit test for header-absent behavior, 4) rerun CI.
Liz Wang: also we should confirm product semantics for Dedicated vs Hosted (does Dedicated always return these headers when reserved capacity configured?). @Samir can you ping product to confirm? :eyes:
Samir Patel: pinged #product with the failing-case details, test logs, and the example. asked product for authoritative behavior matrix.
DevDocs Bot: CI build failed on docs tests — https://ci.redwood-inference/jobs/12345 — failing test: quota_burst_retention (see artifacts).
Mia Chen: leaving quick checklist in thread so we don't lose items: - defensive snippet update - docs note about header optionality + table per deployment - unit test for missing header - add changelog mention for sample change - rerun CI and merge when green
Alex Romero: I can take the unit test and hook it into the docs test runner. I'll add tests/usage/test_quota.py with a mock Response.headers = {} case.
Liz Wang: I'll draft the docs blurb explaining header presence: Hosted: yes for metered accounts; Dedicated: optional depending on reserved capacity and routing; Private (on-prem): depends on integration. Will link to product confirmation once received.
Mia Chen: updated the PR with the defensive snippet and a short helper utility `safe_quota(headers)`; left a comment for reviewers. kicked CI.
Alex Romero: added unit test and one assertion for fallback = -1. pushed to the PR branch.
DevDocs Bot: CI build passed on retest — all docs tests green :tada:
Mia Chen: merged PR. Follow-ups: Liz to add changelog + release note about sample change; Samir to paste product confirmation here for records; Alex to open a tiny follow-up to add a lint example for the helper.
Liz Wang: changelog entry drafted and pushed to docs/changelog/2026-03-24.md.
Samir Patel: product confirmed: Hosted (metered) returns headers; Dedicated returns headers only when public metering proxy is used (customers with reserved-only path may not); Private depends on customer infra. Pasting copy from product: "Quota headers are provided where a metering proxy emits them. For Dedicated deployments with private routing we may not attach headers by default."
Mia Chen: thanks all — closing this thread. I'll add a short note to the docs PR history about the backcompat rationale. :thumbsup:
